question: Should `tools.exec.denylist` force human approval under ordinary `security=full`/`ask=off` while an explicitly authorized elevated-full invocation remains a documented break-glass bypass?
rationale: This intentionally changes the privileged exec authorization contract; source and tests can prove consistency but cannot decide whether elevated-full should bypass operator STOP rules.

options.title: Keep explicit break-glass bypass
options.body: Accept ordinary deny-over-allow enforcement while retaining the narrowly authorized elevated-full bypass and documenting its security implications.

options.title: Make STOP rules absolute
options.body: Require denylist approval even for elevated-full invocations, removing the documented break-glass exception across gateway and node paths.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Do not add the new config and security surface until maintainers define a different exec-policy model.

recommendation.title: Keep explicit break-glass bypass
recommendation.body: Accept ordinary deny-over-allow enforcement while retaining the narrowly authorized elevated-full bypass and documenting its security implications.

likelyOwner.reason: The discussion identifies steipete as the owner for the host exec security contract, and the linked approval issue shows involvement in the same boundary.
